info.name: Waro Public API
info.description:
Public API for Waro Colombia — authenticated via API key (Bearer token).

All requests must include the Authorization header:
  Authorization: Bearer {{api_key}}

The API key encodes the tenant context, so you never need to pass a tenant_id explicitly.

---

## Full checkout flow

1. GET  /v1/restaurant         — fetch the restaurant profile tied to your API key
2. GET  /v1/menu               — list available products (test script saves product_id automatically)
3. GET  /v1/product/{id}       — fetch modifier groups for a product (only when has_modifiers: true)
4. POST /v1/cart/batch         — create a cart with one or more items
5. POST /v1/otp/send           — send a one-time code to the customer's email
6. POST /v1/otp/verify         — verify the code; saves customer_token and customer_id automatically
7. POST /v1/cart/{id}/verify   — bind the authenticated customer to the cart
8. PUT  /v1/cart/{id}/delivery — set the delivery address and order type
9. POST /v1/cart/{id}/checkout — confirm the order and receive an order number

---

## Collection variables

| Variable         | Set by                          | Description                                      |
|------------------|---------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| base_url         | manually                        | API base URL (e.g. https://api.warocol.com)      |
| api_key          | manually                        | API key starting with waro_sk_                   |
| product_id       | GET /v1/menu test script        | UUID of the first product with modifiers         |
| cart_id          | POST /v1/cart/batch test script | UUID of the active cart                          |
| session_id       | POST /v1/cart/batch test script | Session token generated by the backend           |
| customer_token   | POST /v1/otp/verify test script | JWT for the authenticated customer               |
| customer_id      | POST /v1/otp/verify test script | Internal customer UUID (used in address & waros) |
| profile_id       | manually                        | Profile UUID (used in WaRos endpoints)           |
| address_id       | POST /v1/addresses test script  | UUID of the created/selected address             |
| order_id         | POST /v1/cart/checkout script   | UUID of the confirmed order                      |
| test_email       | manually                        | Email used for OTP tests                         |

NOTE: session_id is generated by the backend when the cart is created — never send it in the request body.

item.name: Restaurant and Menu
item.description: Public restaurant profile and menu endpoints. These do not require any customer context — only the API key.

request.description:
Returns the public profile of the restaurant associated with the API key.

Response fields:
- name, description, logo_url
- address, city, phone
- is_open — whether the restaurant is currently accepting orders
- order_types[] — supported types: delivery, pickup

query.description: Optional: filter products by category UUID

request.description:
Returns the public menu with all available products grouped by category.

Each product includes:
- id, name, description, price, image_url
- category_id, category_name
- is_available_online — if false the product cannot be ordered for delivery
- has_modifiers — if true, call GET /v1/product/{id} to fetch modifier groups before adding to cart

Test script automatically saves the first product with has_modifiers=true to the product_id collection variable. Falls back to the first available product if none have modifiers.

Returns the full detail of a single product including its modifier groups.

Only call this endpoint when has_modifiers=true for the product.

Response includes:
- modifier_groups[] — each group has:
  - name, is_required, min_qty, max_qty
  - modifiers[] with id, name, price, is_default
- is_available_online — if false the product cannot be ordered for delivery

When creating a cart, pass the modifier id values from modifiers[] inside the items[].modifiers[] array. Only the id is needed; the backend resolves prices.

exec: console.log(' Group:', g.name, '| required:', g.is_required, '| min:', g.min_qty, '| max:', g.max_qty);

item.name: Cart
item.description:
Cart lifecycle endpoints. The tenant is inferred from the API key and never exposed to callers.

A cart goes through these states:
  open -> verified (after OTP) -> checked_out

Checked-out carts are idempotent: calling checkout again returns 409 with the existing order.

request.description:
Creates a new cart with one or more items in a single request.

Rules:
- Prices are always resolved server-side by product/modifier ID. Do not include unit_price or modifier prices.
- modifiers[] — only the id field is required per modifier. Obtain IDs from GET /v1/product/{id} -> modifier_groups[].modifiers[].id.
- If the product has no modifiers, pass modifiers: [].
- The same product with different modifier combinations is treated as a separate line item.
- order_type: 'delivery' or 'pickup'

Response includes:
- id (cart_id) — saved automatically to cart_id variable
- session_id — saved automatically to session_id variable
- items[] with resolved prices and subtotals
- total_amount

Retrieves the active cart associated with the given session ID.

Useful for restoring an in-progress checkout after a page reload. Returns the same shape as POST /v1/cart/batch.

Updates the delivery configuration for the cart.

Fields:
- order_type: 'delivery' or 'pickup'
- delivery_address_id: UUID of a saved customer address (required when order_type is 'delivery')
- scheduled_time: ISO 8601 timestamp for scheduled delivery, or null for ASAP
- delivery_instructions: free text note for the courier

Removes a specific item from the cart by its item UUID.

The item UUID is returned in the items[] array of POST /v1/cart/batch or GET /v1/cart/session/{id}.

Removes all items from the cart, effectively emptying it.

The cart record itself is preserved in an empty state. To abandon the cart entirely, simply stop using the session.

Binds an already-authenticated customer to the cart. Requires both the API key and the customer JWT.

Use this when the customer has an active session (valid cookie or stored token) and does not need to go through OTP again.

Pass the token from POST /v1/otp/verify in the X-Customer-Token header.

Confirms the cart as a placed order. The cart must have been verified via OTP or an existing session before calling this endpoint.

This operation is idempotent: calling it a second time returns HTTP 409 with the already-created order.

Response includes:
- order_id, order_number
- total_amount, order_type
- pickup_pin — 4-digit code shown to the customer for in-store pickup orders
- estimated_ready_at — estimated preparation time

item.name: OTP
item.description:
Customer identity verification via one-time password (OTP) sent to email.

Flow:
1. POST /v1/otp/send   — sends a 6-digit code to the customer's email (tied to the cart)
2. POST /v1/otp/verify — verifies the code; returns a signed JWT (customer_token)
3. POST /v1/otp/resend — resends the code if the customer did not receive it (60 s cooldown)

On successful verification:
- Browser clients receive an HttpOnly cookie (waro_customer_session)
- Non-browser clients receive customer_token in the response body

The test script on /verify saves customer_token and customer_id automatically.

request.description:
Sends a 6-digit OTP code to the customer's email address.

The code is valid for 10 minutes. A new code can be requested via /v1/otp/resend after a 60-second cooldown.

Fields:
- email: customer's email address
- cart_id: UUID of the active cart (ties the OTP session to the cart)

Verifies the OTP code sent to the customer's email and issues a signed JWT.

On success:
- Sets an HttpOnly cookie waro_customer_session (for browser clients)
- Returns customer_token in the response body (for non-browser / API clients)
- Returns customer_id — the internal UUID for this customer in the tenant
- Returns profile_id — the global profile UUID used in WaRos endpoints

Test script automatically saves customer_token and customer_id to collection variables.

Errors:
- 400 — invalid or expired code
- 429 — too many failed attempts

Resends the OTP code to the same email address.

Enforces a 60-second cooldown between resend requests to prevent abuse. Returns 429 if called within the cooldown window.

Same request shape as POST /v1/otp/send.

item.name: Customer Validation
item.description: Validates whether a customer is eligible to place an order. Checks the tenant blacklist, loyalty tier constraints, and spending limits.

request.description:
Checks whether the customer is allowed to place an order at this tenant.

Fields:
- phone_number: E.164 format (e.g. +573001234567)
- cart_total: order total in COP (used to evaluate spending limits by tier)

Response includes:
- is_eligible: true / false
- reason: human-readable explanation if not eligible (blacklisted, tier limit exceeded, etc.)
- tier: customer's current loyalty tier

item.name: Addresses
item.description:
Customer delivery address management. A customer can store up to 5 addresses. One address can be marked as the default, which is pre-selected at checkout.

All write operations require the customer_id obtained from POST /v1/otp/verify.

request.description:
Creates a new delivery address for the customer.

Rules:
- Maximum 5 active addresses per customer. Returns HTTP 422 if the limit is reached.
- If is_default=true, all other addresses for this customer are automatically unset as default.
- address_type: 'home', 'work', or 'other'
- latitude/longitude: optional, used for map display and delivery zone validation

Test script automatically saves the new address UUID to the address_id collection variable.

Returns all active (non-deleted) addresses for the customer.

Response:
- addresses[]: list ordered by default first, then most recent
- total: count of active addresses
- default_address_id: UUID of the current default address, or null

query.description: Ownership validation — must match the address owner

request.description:
Partially updates an address. Only the fields included in the request body are modified; omitted fields are left unchanged.

Updatable fields:
- address_line1, address_line2
- city, state, postal_code, country
- latitude, longitude
- is_default — setting true here also unsets all other defaults
- address_type: 'home', 'work', 'other'
- delivery_notes

customer_id query param is required for ownership validation.

query.description: Ownership validation — must match the address owner

request.description:
Sets this address as the customer's default delivery address.

Automatically unsets any previously set default for this customer. Returns the full updated address object.

customer_id query param is required for ownership validation.

query.description: Ownership validation — must match the address owner

request.description:
Soft-deletes the address by setting deleted_at. The record is preserved in the database but no longer returned by the list endpoint.

If the deleted address was the default and other addresses exist, the most recently created address is automatically promoted as the new default.

customer_id query param is required for ownership validation.

item.name: Sales
item.description: Sales data and metrics for the tenant. All endpoints accept date range filters and return data scoped to the API key's tenant.

request.description:
Returns a paginated list of orders within the specified date range.

Filters:
- status: null (all) | 'completed' | 'cancelled' | 'pending'
- paymentMethod: null (all) | 'cash' | 'card' | 'transfer'
- sortField: 'created_at' | 'total_amount'
- sortDirection: 'asc' | 'desc'

Dates are interpreted in the given timezone.

Returns aggregated sales metrics with optional time/dimension grouping.

groupBy options:
- null — summary totals only (revenue, order count, average ticket)
- 'weekday' — breakdown by day of week (Mon–Sun)
- 'hour' — breakdown by hour of day (0–23)
- 'product' — revenue and quantity per product
- 'payment' — breakdown by payment method
- 'ticket' — ticket size distribution

Returns the full detail of a single order including all line items.

Response includes:
- order header (status, order_type, total, timestamps)
- items[] with product name, quantity, unit_price, modifiers, subtotal
- payment info
- customer summary

item.name: Menu API
item.description: Detailed menu data for internal tooling and CLI use. Includes ingredients, recipes, and modifier groups with full configuration.

request.description:
Returns a paginated list of products with optional related data.

Filters:
- isAvailable: true | false | null (all)
- categoryId: filter by category UUID

Expansion flags (set to true to include in response):
- includeIngredients — raw ingredient list per product
- includeRecipeBases — recipe base compositions
- includeModifiers — modifier groups with options

Returns a paginated list of recipes (recipe bases) with their ingredient compositions.

Filters:
- isActive: true | false | null (all)

Response includes per recipe:
- id, name, unit, yield_quantity
- ingredients[] with ingredient_id, name, quantity, unit, unit_cost
- total_cost — calculated cost based on current ingredient prices

Returns a paginated list of all modifier groups with their modifier options.

Response includes per group:
- id, name, is_required, min_qty, max_qty
- modifiers[] with id, name, price, is_default, is_active

item.name: Customers
item.description: Customer list, detail, order history, and aggregate metrics for the tenant.

request.description:
Returns a paginated list of customers for the tenant.

Filters:
- search: partial match on name, email, or phone
- dateFrom / dateTo: filter by first purchase date

Sorting:
- sortField: 'total_spent' | 'order_count' | 'last_order_date' | 'avg_ticket'
- sortDirection: 'asc' | 'desc'

Response per customer:
- customer_id — use this as customerId in /v1/customers/detail and /v1/customers/orders
- name, phone, order_count, total_spent, avg_ticket, last_order_date, waros_balance

Returns the full profile for a single customer along with a summary of their activity.

customerId must be the customer_id field from POST /v1/customers — not the OTP profile UUID.

Response includes:
- customer: name, email, phone, total_orders, total_spent, first_purchase, last_purchase
- orders[]: recent orders (paginated with limit/offset)
- waros_summary: current balance, lifetime earned, lifetime spent

Returns a paginated order history for a single customer.

customerId must be the customer_id field from POST /v1/customers.

includeItems:
- false (default) — returns order headers only (faster)
- true — includes full items[] per order via a batched query (no N+1)

Returns aggregate customer metrics and top customer rankings.

groupBy options:
- null — totals only (new customers, returning rate, average LTV)
- 'date' — new vs returning customers per day
- 'weekday' — customer activity by day of week
- 'month' — monthly customer acquisition

item.name: Analytics
item.description: Advanced analytical endpoints for menu performance, customer behavior, and operational health. All date filters are optional — omitting them analyzes the full available history.

request.description:
BCG matrix analysis of the menu. Classifies products into four quadrants based on popularity (order frequency) vs. profitability (margin):

- Stars — high popularity, high margin (promote and protect)
- Plowhorses — high popularity, low margin (optimize cost or raise price)
- Puzzles — low popularity, high margin (improve visibility or bundle)
- Dogs — low popularity, low margin (consider removing)

Response includes the quadrant classification and the underlying metrics per product.

Returns food cost analysis for the selected period with period-over-period comparison.

compareTo:
- 'previous_period' — compares against the immediately preceding period of the same length
- 'previous_year' — compares against the same date range one year prior

Response includes:
- total_cost, total_revenue, food_cost_percentage
- per-product cost breakdown
- delta vs. the comparison period

Returns the most recent operational alerts detected by the analytics engine.

Alerts are automatically generated when the system detects anomalies such as:
- Unusual drop in sales volume
- Product with no sales in an unexpected window
- Ingredient cost spikes
- High cart abandonment rate

Each alert includes a severity level, description, and the affected entity.

Runs a data quality audit on the tenant's configuration and returns a list of issues found.

Checks include:
- Products missing cost data (blocks food cost analytics)
- Ingredients without unit prices
- Products with no sales in the last 90 days
- Missing product images
- Modifier groups with no active options

Returns a severity-ranked list of issues with remediation hints.

Customer retention cohort analysis. Groups customers by the week or month they made their first purchase, then tracks what percentage of each cohort returned in subsequent periods.

Fields:
- period: 'weekly' | 'monthly'
- periods: number of periods to analyze (1–24)

Response shape:
- period: the granularity used
- cohorts[]: each entry has a cohort_date, size (customers acquired), and retention[] array with the return rate per subsequent period

RFM (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) segmentation of the customer base.

Each customer is scored 1–N on three dimensions and classified into a named segment:
- Champions — bought recently, buy often, spent the most
- Loyal — buy regularly with good spending
- At Risk — used to buy often but have gone quiet
- Hibernating — low recency, low frequency
- Lost — haven't purchased in a very long time

segments: number of quantile buckets per dimension (2–10, default 5 = quintiles).

Response includes per-segment counts, average scores, and the full customer list per segment.

Identifies customers at risk of churning using a personalized inactivity model.

A customer is flagged when their days since last purchase exceed (threshold_multiplier x their personal average inter-visit interval). Each customer has their own threshold — a customer who normally orders every 7 days is flagged at a different point than one who orders monthly.

Fields:
- threshold_multiplier: how many times the personal average before flagging (default 2.0)
- min_orders: minimum order count to include in analysis (filters out one-time buyers)
- limit / offset: pagination

Response includes per customer: days_since_last_order, avg_interval_days, personal_threshold, risk_score.

Returns WaRos loyalty program activity analytics.

groupBy:
- 'customer' — points earned and spent per customer
- 'day' — daily totals for points issued and redeemed
- 'week' — weekly aggregation

Response includes a summary (total issued, total redeemed, net outstanding) and the grouped breakdown.

item.name: Financial
item.description: Product-level financial analysis: margin, cost, and profitability. Useful for pricing decisions and food cost control.

request.description:
Returns financial performance metrics per product for the specified look-back period.

Fields:
- period: number of days to analyze (1–730, default 365)
- category: filter by category name (partial match)
- minMargin: only return products with margin >= this value (0.0–1.0)
- sortBy: 'margin' | 'revenue' | 'cost' | 'quantity'

Response includes:
- products[]: per-product cost, price, margin %, revenue, quantity sold
- metrics: overall food cost %, top and bottom performers
- categories[]: aggregated by category
- insights[]: auto-generated recommendations
- filters: the applied filter values echoed back

item.name: WaRos
item.description:
WaRos loyalty points endpoints. Points are earned on every order and can be redeemed for discounts.

These endpoints use profile_id (the global customer profile UUID), not customer_id (which is tenant-scoped). The profile_id is returned by POST /v1/otp/verify.

request.description:
Returns the WaRos loyalty summary for a single customer.

profileId is the global profile UUID — obtained from POST /v1/otp/verify (not the tenant-scoped customer_id).

Response:
- profile_id
- current_balance — spendable points
- lifetime_earned — total points ever earned
- lifetime_spent — total points ever redeemed
- recent_transactions[]: last N transactions

Batch endpoint that returns current WaRos balances for up to 250 profiles in a single request.

Designed for bulk operations such as populating a customer list view with loyalty balances without making individual requests per customer.

profileIds: array of global profile UUIDs (max 250).

Response: balances[] with one entry per requested profileId.

Estimates how many WaRos points the customer would earn for a given purchase amount.

Used to display the points preview at checkout before the order is confirmed.

Fields:
- totalAmount: order total in COP
- customerId: optional; if provided, applies the customer's tier multiplier

Response:
- estimated_waros: points that would be awarded
- system_enabled: whether the WaRos program is active for this tenant
- breakdown: base rate, tier multiplier, bonus rules applied

Returns a paginated transaction history for a customer's WaRos wallet.

profileId is the global profile UUID from POST /v1/otp/verify.

transactionType filter:
- null — all transactions
- 'earned' — points awarded from orders
- 'manual' — points manually assigned by staff

Response:
- profile_id
- total_count: total transactions matching the filter
- transactions[]: each entry has type, points, description, order_id (if earned), created_at
